source_title: Issues in Restructuring of Sovereign Domestic Debt — Background Paper
source_finding: The Greek debt exchange was completed on 12 March 2012. The IMF reports a 53.5 percent nominal face-value reduction.
payment_default_finding: The IMF describes this debt exchange as pre-emptive, with no payments missed during the exchange.
restructuring_finding: Sovereign debt restructuring is established for the March 2012 Greek PSI transaction.
limitation: The finding concerns the PSI exchange, not every Greek sovereign obligation or every date in the Greek debt crisis.

source_title: Restructuring Credit Event Has Occurred with Respect to The Hellenic Republic
source_finding: ISDA's EMEA Determinations Committee unanimously determined that a Restructuring Credit Event had occurred under the applicable CDS definitions.
restructuring_finding: The determination followed the exercise of collective action clauses that reduced affected bondholders' rights to receive payments.
limitation: A CDS restructuring credit event is a contractual classification under derivatives definitions. It must not automatically be equated with a missed-payment default.

source_title: Sovereign Debt Restructuring — Recent Developments and Implications for the Fund's Legal and Policy Framework
source_finding: The IMF explains that restructuring can qualify as a CDS credit event even when the debt exchange occurs before a payment default.
payment_default_finding: A pre-default debt exchange can trigger a CDS credit event.
restructuring_finding: The Greek restructuring involved collective action procedures that bound affected creditors.
cds_credit_event_finding: The Greek CDS was triggered following activation of the collective action procedure.
limitation: This is an explanatory policy paper, not the ISDA Determinations Committee's primary decision.
